explanation: A class template declaration in C++ defines a blueprint for creating classes parameterized by types. It allows the programmer to write generic, reusable class definitions that can operate with any data type specified at instantiation time. This feature is fundamental for generic programming, enabling code flexibility, type safety, and compile-time polymorphism, especially within the Standard Template Library (STL) and modern C++ idioms.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates a class template 'PointerToBinaryFunction' parameterized by three types: Arg1, Arg2, and Result. The class defines an operator() to perform an operation (here, addition) on two arguments of types Arg1 and Arg2, returning a Result type. In main(), an instance is created with specific types (int, int, int), and the operator() is invoked to compute the sum. This showcases how class templates enable generic, type-safe class definitions that can be instantiated with different types, exemplifying the core concept of class template declaration in modern C++.
